newsitem.title: USA: Lott gives details of Clinton-Congress summit.
newsitem.headline: Lott gives details of Clinton-Congress summit.

text.p: Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott gave details Friday of plans for an unusual summit meeting next Tuesday between President Clinton and congressional leaders of both parties.

The 11 a.m. meeting in the ornate President's Room on tne Senate side of the U.S. Capitol follows Clinton's submission of his fiscal 1998 budget and his Feb. 4 State of the Union address laying out his program.
Lott and House Speaker Newt Gingrich had invited Clinton to talks last Wednesday but Clinton was out of town that day.
The invitation was for a discussion of what the two Republicans leaders called five areas of "the critical agenda facing our country."

These were balancing the budget by the year 2002, providing tax relief for working Americans, improving education at the local level, fighting crime and drugs and disposing safely of toxic and nuclear wastes.

Also at the meeting will be Vice President Al Gore, Sen. Strom Thurmond, President Pro Tem of the Senate, House Republican Leader Dick Armey, Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle, House Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt, Senate Republican Whip Don Nickles, Senate Democratic Whip Wendell Ford, House Republican Whip Tom DeLay and House Democratic Whip David Bonior.
